title: Git authority and executable ontology can coexist without split brain
claim: With Git as canonical authority, Project Ontology can rebuild deterministically, execute governed changes through versioned Git mutations, detect stale/conflicting writes and preserve historical bindings without becoming a competing source of truth.
null_hypothesis: Making the ontology executable creates a second mutable truth store whose state can diverge from Git or lose concurrency/history semantics.
rivals: A Git-native workflow without an ontology projection is sufficient and safer.
Rebuild determinism holds only on happy paths, not concurrent/stale histories.
mechanism: Treat ontology state as a deterministic projection of versioned Git artifacts and require every canonical mutation to carry a base version and produce a Git commit/change record.
scope: Project Ontology canonical state, H15-H22 contracts/evidence and generated commit/action interleavings.
predictions: Clean rebuild from the same Git commit produces identical canonical ontology state hash.
Every durable Project Action that changes canonical state produces a Git-visible versioned artifact.
Stale writes never silently overwrite newer canonical state.
Historical evidence/verdict bindings remain associated with original commit/version after later changes.
falsifiers: Same Git commit rebuilds to different canonical state.
Canonical ontology state changes without a Git-visible change.
Generated stale write causes a lost update.
Historical evidence silently rebinds to a later contract/version.

experiment.summary: Property/state-machine test of Git commits, ontology rebuilds, governed changes, stale bases, merges and conflicts.
steps: Generate repository histories and Project Actions from random valid bases.
Rebuild projection repeatedly and compare hashes.
Generate concurrent compatible and conflicting changes.
Verify optimistic concurrency/conflict behavior and historical references.
Inject nondeterministic rebuild and stale-write bugs.

oracle: Simplified immutable Git DAG/reference model plus deterministic projection function defined independently of runtime storage.
baseline: Direct Git-native mutation workflow with no executable ontology store.

support_if: 100% rebuild hash equality for identical Git commits.
0 silent lost updates in generated concurrency corpus.
reject_if: Any split-brain, nondeterministic rebuild, silent lost update or history rebinding is observed.
inconclusive_if: Concurrency corpus lacks stale-base and conflicting-change classes.
invalid_if: Runtime database is used as the oracle for Git canonical state.

python_hypothesis_role.strategy: State machine generates commit DAG operations, base revisions, Project Actions, rebuilds, merges and conflicts.
python_hypothesis_role.mutation_proof: Inject timestamp-dependent projection, missing base-version check and history-rebinding bug; suite must shrink/detect them.

stop_conditions: If Git and ontology cannot maintain one-way canonical authority without special manual reconciliation, reject before adding more self-hosted actions.
